a4_lock: The relay iron goes into the ninth socket and the socket takes it the way a lock takes its own key, without argument or ceremony. The door's breathing stops in the middle of a count. Eight irons and a ninth, all nine warm, the frame taking up the load, and behind it nothing moving at all for the first time in four months.
a4_break_die: The tally-die is carried back to the cutting-shop and broken across its own anvil in four strokes, and dwarf steel comes apart in a way that dwarf steel is not supposed to come apart. Vurma goes over the floor on her knees afterwards twice, collecting fragments into a sack, and does not accept help with it.
a4_take_ring: The ninth hand's ring lies on the desk beside Ferrin's book, warm and exactly sized for whoever picks it up. The arithmetic beside it is not complicated: nine irons will hold the lid without a keeper right up until something decides to test the arrangement. A count kept honestly by somebody who hates the work is the difference.
a4_ring_on: The ring goes on, and the count arrives at the back of the skull like a schedule of payments read aloud by a patient clerk. It is not a voice and it is not a compulsion; it is an obligation, and it has dates in it. The captain of the Ninth Sword stands in a courier chapel and understands the shape of the rest of a life.
a4_unmake: This is the decision to unmake the Compact at the second door, and it deserves being said out loud before anybody touches anything. Eight irons in eight warm sockets. Nine hundred years of instalments paid by people who were never consulted. And five people standing in front of the only working arrangement anybody has ever managed with what is behind it.
a4_one_at_a_time: One iron out, and the door leans a quarter of an inch outward against its frame. Two, and the stone around the sockets begins visibly to sweat. Three, and the door speaks in the road-paymaster's voice and asks, with genuine courtesy, whether the company has come to settle the account or merely to increase it.
a4_reseat: Three irons go back into three sockets, put there by hands that are not remotely steady, and the door settles with the sound of a held breath let out slowly. The paymaster's voice thanks the company by name, all five names, pronounced correctly and in the order they came down the stair. Then it stops.
a4_wedge: The relay iron is driven crosswise through the socket ring rather than into it, dwarf iron biting on dwarf iron until the whole ring is locked into a single piece. No hand can draw it and no keeper can count it, which is the entire point of the exercise. It is crude and permanent and in nobody's written orders, and Vurma says she would have done it first.
a4_open: A hand's width of the second door, held open on the pick haft with Dellach's boot braced hard against the frame. Warm air comes out of the gap in a rhythm that is not wind and never was. There is light on the other side of it, and the light is not lamplight, and it has no source that anybody can identify.
a4_looked: Behind the second door is not a beast in a lair but a hall the size of the mountain, with something at the far end of it too large to resolve into a shape. Standing in rows in front of that, in Warden cloaks and Reckoning habits and dwarf mail, are four thousand people. Every one of them is counting, and they are not synchronised.
a4_lamp_through: A lit lamp is set through the gap on a rope and lowered a foot. It burns steadily for four seconds, then goes out from the wick downward, which is not a thing lamps do. Then it comes back up the rope, relit by nobody at all, and the colour of the flame is noticeably better than it was before.
a4_closed_unlooked: The door is eased shut on nothing seen and the haft withdrawn, and the count resumes exactly where it left off without comment. Five people stand in a dwarf gallery having decided together not to know something. Each of them will privately want to know it for the rest of their lives, and two of them will eventually ask.
a4_carry: The arithmetic works from the other direction as well. Eight irons hold the lid for as long as nobody tests it, but the ninth is the count itself, and a count that cannot be kept is a debt that cannot be collected. Kar Duhn's ninth iron is already in your pack, and this one would make two.
a4_wrap_iron: Salt-cloth, then oilcloth, then the middle of the pack beside the first one, arranged by Ilsabet so that the two irons do not touch each other at any point. The whole march's attention arrives and settles on five people who now hold two of the Compact's nine counts in a single bag, and who are walking out with them.
a4_withdraw: The honest option is said out loud in front of the second door by Nyre, who has been assembling it since the chapel and delivers it in four sentences. This arrangement is nine hundred years old. It is a Warden matter and a crime by her own order, and five people with one commission do not get to be its hinge.
a4_take_ledger: Back up to the road office for four pounds of Warden record that Orr will read carefully and the Reckoning will want burnt. The lamp above the desk is still lit. Behind the desk the clerk's cubby is exactly as it was, with the plaster tally running all the way to the ceiling and the hole still breathing warm air.
a4_out: Four hundred steps up, and the march has changed its mind about the company somewhere on the way. The flights are longer than they were coming down, the stair-shrine's ninth niche is warm again, and all nine lamps in the tower gallery are lit and trimmed. At the top of it the gate leaf has come to within a thumb's width of shut.
a4_force_gate: Five people, a pick haft, a Warden's shield used as a fulcrum, and eleven minutes of the worst work any of them has ever done. The leaf gives an inch at a time against a pressure that is not weight and is not wind. Whatever is applying it is not interested in being negotiated with and is not in any hurry.
a4_chute_out: The ventilation shaft from below is forty feet of dwarf cut with half its staples missing at the top. The cistern room behind you is filling steadily and audibly. The lamps in the tower gallery are going out one at a time, from the far end, working methodically toward the head of the relay stair.
a4_postern_out: Out by the mason's postern into Lamp Road air, with the lead seal broken behind you and the corridor beyond lighting itself politely, one niche at a time, all the way back to the stair. It has the manner of a house showing a guest to the door and then watching, from the window, to make sure they leave.
a4_file_out: The ninth hour is waited out in the oil store, and then the file forms on the stair below: nine lamps lifted, the count started, everything precisely on schedule. The Ninth Sword walks out of Sixteen Mile in the middle of it with the rhythm right and every hand out of sight, and nobody in the file turns round.
a4_moorback: The Lamp Road at the first hour, with the Marchgate behind you and Rell's Gate half a day up the paving. The company carries whatever it decided to carry, and the barrow is lighter than it was. Nyre asks the question that has to be settled before anybody speaks to a Warden, which is not what happened but what you are going to say happened.
a4_bothy: Two days at the fourth station with a working flue and no watch to keep, which the charts describe as safe and which turns out to be exactly that. Kettle sleeps eleven hours without moving once. Dellach's hands come back to him by the second evening, and Ilsabet writes the whole account out twice in case one copy burns.
a4_council: The company council convenes on a lamp-station bench and runs for an hour. Dellach argues for the Warden and the written record; Nyre for her own order's hearing and the naming of Vask; Kettle for the west road and no names at all. Ilsabet argues for whichever choice keeps the fewest copies of the truth in the fewest hands.
a4_boy: There is a promise to keep, made in a lamp gallery in front of witnesses and written down in Nyre's book with the hour beside it. Keeping it means going back down to Sixteen Mile for a Reckoning novice, into a tower the company has just spent everything it had in order to leave. Dellach is already checking the postern route.
a4_gallowmere: Rell's Gate in a thaw, and everybody is waiting. The Warden's tower has a lamp burning at the wrong hour, a Reckoning coach with southern horses stands in the yard, and the Rooks are pretending not to watch the road. At the gate shrine Prior Vask is lighting candles in nines for a brother nobody has yet reported dead.
a4_mother: Prior Vask at the gate shrine, told the truth in a thawing street by a captain who has rehearsed the words for two days and gets them wrong regardless. She has known since autumn. She has been requisitioning the deliveries herself, to keep the count from falling behind, and she explains her reasoning without being asked for it.
a4_report: Captain Sabinne Orr reads it twice, all of it, without asking a single question in the meantime. Then she squares the pages, sets them down, and asks the only three questions that matter to a Warden of the Deep Road: what is shut, what is loose, and what exactly is in the company's pack at this moment.
a4_record: The written report will outlive everybody in the room: dated, signed by five hands, and sealed to the Warden archive at Rell's Gate before the week is out. It requires the captain of the Ninth Sword to set down in plain words what was done to the second door and by whom. The hours are to be attached to each entry.
a4_name_halloway: The Reckoning hearing convenes in the chapter house with three priors down from the south, and Vask sits at the end of the table taking her own minutes in a steady hand. Nyre stands up as a sister of the Reckoning to say that her brother did not act alone, and that the requisitions are in her prior's handwriting.
a4_causeway: The last mile of Lamp Road into Rell's Gate comes up in a thaw, with water running off the rock in sheets. The gatehouse stands ahead, the tower lamp burns at an hour that means somebody is waiting up, and a Reckoning coach with southern horses is standing in the yard with its curtains drawn and its driver still on the box.
a4_ahead: Kettle is back from the gate inside eleven minutes with a list, delivered flat and in order of importance to the company. The Rooks are in the yard doing nothing, badly, in the wet. A Reckoning clerk is taking names at the chapter house door, and eleven Warden cloaks on the gate do not fit the men inside them.
a4_tower: The Warden's anteroom at Rell's Gate, with wet cloaks steaming on the pegs and the report copied fair in Ilsabet's hand. You read it through once more while a clerk pretends not to watch the pack that has not left the captain's shoulder since Hollowmarch, and has not been set down anywhere, including overnight.
e_a4_completion: Two irons kept, wrapped, and entered on the record as company property held in trust, which takes Orr's clerk three attempts to phrase in a way the archive will accept. Her letter goes south over her own seal that evening to the wardens of the spine. Two of the Compact's nine counts are now unkeepable by anybody at all, which has never once been true in nine hundred years. And Ferrin's book lies open on a Warden table at the page that lists the third door, under the spine of the Wyrmreach where the wyrm itself is, with a date against it that falls at the thaw.
e_a4_win_charter: The Deep Road oath is converted into a standing Warden charter with a company seal and a road writ, and the Ninth Sword is entered in the Warden roll as a name rather than a hire. The first order issued under it reads, in Orr's own hand: hold the march, and report the hour of every lamp.
e_a4_win_plain: The road-book is delivered, the relay iron is handed across a Warden table and locked into a Warden strongbox, and the fee is paid in full with the hazard added on without argument. There is a door under Hollowmarch that is shut tonight and will still be shut in the morning. The tower will be garrisoned again by summer, with lamps on the proper hours.
e_a4_win_book: Eleven hundred pages of instalments in nine hands are laid on a Warden captain's desk, which makes them her problem, her career, and no longer the company's business. Orr reads the last four months twice over without speaking once. She has the slow attention of somebody recognising a hand she has countersigned herself, repeatedly, for four years.
e_a4_win_testify: Prior Enna Vask is named to her face in front of three southern priors, and her own requisitions are matched to the road account by Nyre in open hearing. She does not deny any of it, which surprises nobody in the room except the priors. An order discovers that its frontier chapter has been settling debts in people since before the ice came.
e_a4_wedge_win: A socket ring locked into a single piece by a relay iron driven crosswise, reported in plain words and copied twice for the archive. A Warden request goes south the same week for masons and a mining engineer at Warden expense. What the company did cannot be undone by any hand, and cannot be trusted forever by anybody who knows metal.
e_a4_win_boy: The promise is kept. In at the postern at dusk, the lamp gallery empty with all nine lamps lit and trimmed, and Brother Cull found asleep in the oil store where he had been hiding for two days on half a loaf and a jar of water. He goes out over Dellach's shoulder into thawing air, and Nyre closes the entry in her book.
e_a4_silent: A short honest report that says the door is shut and then stops there, with the fee paid and the company thanked and released before dark. Four people each know that a decision was taken in a dwarf gallery. Nine hundred years of arithmetic was left out of a Warden's file deliberately, and none of the four ever raises the matter again.
e_a4_surety: The relay iron is handed to the Reckoning as surety and entered in its register under a number, which makes it the safest place on the road and also the one place the Compact has always been able to reach. The company keeps a receipt. The receipt will be worth precisely what the paper it is written on is worth.
e_a4_keeper_office: It goes into a Warden file in the captain's own hand: the door is shut, all nine irons are seated, and the count is kept by the captain of the Ninth Sword. There will be a visit to the Marchgate every ninth night, at the ninth hour, for the rest of a life that now has a schedule attached to it.
e_a4_open_admitted: The truth is entered in the record to the inch, as the oath requires. The tower is evacuated within the hour, Rell's Gate posts its own evacuation order by noon, and a company that did the honest thing sits in the yard watching a road town load its carts. The road is closed at both ends by the following week.
e_a4_reseat_end: Three irons drawn and reseated, written down in exactly those words, with a Warden clerk copying the entry out twice for the archive. Then Orr asks the question that nobody in the room can answer and everybody has already considered. Whether a socket that has been emptied once holds the same as a socket that has never been emptied at all.
e_a4_withdrew: The file records that the company reached the second door, described it accurately, touched nothing at all, and came back out. It is the most defensible sentence in the Rell's Gate archive. It is also the one the Ninth Sword will be asked about in every station house on the Deep Road for the next nine years.
e_a4_fee: The fee is paid for the road-book with no questions invited and none asked by anybody in the tower, and the company is out of the gatehouse before dark. The money is split five ways on the road south. There is an understanding between them, never spoken aloud, that Hollowmarch has become somebody else's arithmetic entirely.
e_a4_bought: The charts, the hours, the cadence and the company's silence are sold to Vasse Corrow for three hundred crowns and a promise. At the thaw a chartered company goes down the Lamp Road with fifteen people who were told the easy version of the story. Six of them come back up, and none of the six will discuss the hours.
e_a4_south: Rell's Gate is skirted and the west road taken over the shoulder with the pack still packed. No report, no fee, no charter, and two of the Compact's nine irons travelling further from their sockets every day in the luggage of five people who have agreed, in some detail, never to discuss the matter again.
e_a4_split: An argument on a lamp-station bench is allowed to run until it stops being an argument. Kettle goes west that afternoon with her share. Nyre returns to her order with her own account of the chapel, Dellach walks into the tower alone with his, and the Ninth Sword ends not at a door but in a disagreement about paperwork.
e_a4_mother_stay: An afternoon at a gate shrine with a prior lighting candles in nines for the brother whose deliveries she was requisitioning herself. It is the right place for a captain to be and entirely the wrong place for this captain today. Orr waits four hours and then writes in her file that the company did not present itself.
e_a4_jam_fail: The relay iron is hammered in at an angle to jam the socket permanently, and it works. It also cracks the stone collar around the socket, and a ring of nine that has held for nine hundred years discovers, all at once and in front of witnesses, that it is now a ring of eight and one wound.
e_a4_unmade: Eight irons are pulled in well under a minute, and the company runs for a stair that is four hundred steps long. It is a plan that requires the door to open slowly. The second door has been waiting nine hundred years for exactly this opportunity and sees no reason whatsoever to be slow about taking it.
e_a4_opened: The fourth iron is drawn while the paymaster's voice is still being courteous about the account, and then the fifth. After that no further decisions are required of anybody standing in the gallery. The arrangement has concluded, and the accounts are being settled in the order in which they were originally opened, starting at the top.
e_a4_asked: The question is asked through three empty sockets, and it is answered in full: itemised, with dates and running totals and a note about interest. The figure is one that the company is standing inside of. The door explains, without any heat at all, that a debt does not require the consent of the instalment.
e_a4_wedge_fail: A shoulder is put against a wedged door to establish whether the work holds, which it does, entirely, and would have gone on doing indefinitely. In the same second the thing on the other side puts its own weight against the same door. It does so out of what can only reasonably be described as professional curiosity.
e_a4_spoke: One sentence is spoken through a hand's width of open door, in common speech, quite politely, with the pick haft still braced. The reply does not arrive as sound. It arrives as arithmetic: the company counted, priced, scheduled, and entered against an instalment which the records show as falling due immediately.
e_a4_in_for_people: The door is pushed wide and five people walk into a hall the size of a mountain to bring out four thousand who are standing in rows, counting. It is the most defensible decision anybody makes anywhere in this story. It adds five to the rows, adjusts the schedule by nothing at all, and changes nothing else.
e_a4_lamp: An arm goes through the gap to take back a lamp that has been relit by nobody. The lamp is handed over properly, into the hand that reached for it, by something that has been waiting nine hundred years for a transaction it did not itself have to initiate. It is careful not to spill any of the oil.
e_a4_moor: The relay iron is sunk in the cistern dip on the way up the road, which solves the problem for one winter. At the spring load the water line drops a foot and a Guild train's water detail finds a strip of warm metal on the bottom and sells it at Rell's Gate for two coppers to a clerk with southern horses.
e_a4_bait: The relay iron is carried openly up the Lamp Road as an invitation, on the theory that whatever wants it must come out into lamplight and negotiate for it. On the second night the company discovers that it does not have to come out at all and never has. It does not consider a lit dwarf road to be outside anything.
e_a4_burn_lamps: Nine lamps are smashed and left burning in the Marchgate arch as a gesture on the way out, which feels entirely justified at the time and is discussed with some satisfaction for two days. The road's answer does not arrive that night. It arrives nine nights later at Rell's Gate, at the third hour, with its own lamps and its own list.
e_a4_sell_knowledge: Everything the company learned under the mountain is sold to Vasse Corrow in a thawing yard for good coin and no receipt of any kind. The commission goes back to the tower unfulfilled with an excuse that Orr does not believe and cannot disprove. A chartered banner goes down the Lamp Road a week later, and the hours have changed again by then.
e_a4_ledger_lingered: The plaster tally is chiselled off the cubby wall on the grounds that it is evidence, and evidence is what wins arguments with Wardens. The work takes eleven minutes from the first stroke to the last one. That is about eight minutes longer than the clerk's own arrangement allowed for with whatever comes to read his wall on the hour.
e_a4_sat_down: A captain sits down on the two hundredth step because the legs have finished arguing about it. The company will not leave without its captain, which is what a company is for and why the arrangement works at all. The stair has been getting longer all evening, and it is in no hurry whatsoever.
e_a4_forced_shut: The gate leaf is held on a shield fulcrum while five names are called through it in order, which is precisely what the shield's dead owner scratched a warning about on the inside face. The fifth name is answered from behind the leaf in the captain's own voice. It arrives with the correct inflection and about a second early.
e_a4_chute_out_fall: The strongest goes up the shaft first to haul the others, which puts one set of hands at the top and four sets of boots on staples that are half missing. The fourth staple from the top has been waiting all day for exactly this weight, in exactly this order, and it does not have to wait any longer.
e_a4_file_kept: The file is stayed with to the end of the count, because it is only nine and the rhythm is easy and the company is very nearly out of the tower. The ninth number arrives on the paving in open road air with the Lamp Road plainly visible ahead, and then the count starts again from one without any gap at all.
e_a4_boy_lost: The gate leaf is taken because it is faster and because the novice needs an hour of the morning to walk out in. The leaf is wide enough for one person going quickly, and then it is not wide enough for anybody. The company keeps its promise as far as the threshold, and Nyre writes down the hour it failed.
e_a4_ambushed: Kettle's report proves accurate in every particular, as her reports generally do. The Rooks are in the yard, a Reckoning coach stands at the chapter house, and eleven Warden cloaks on the gate do not fit the men wearing them. The company walks into Rell's Gate regardless, because there is nowhere else on this road left to walk to.
e_a4_left_with_clerk: A fair copy of everything is left on a clerk's desk with five names on it and no witness to the handing over. Orr reads it eleven days later, by which time the Reckoning coach has been back to the chapter house twice and left again, and the company is four days west with the pack still packed.
